brief.headline: Push for 45-day payment terms (from 30) and a 5–10% price cut — they're 100% a trader, so push to maker's price, and you're 1.19% of their revenue

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 5–10% price cut to get closer to what a manufacturer would charge
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc on induction-wad caps (market research shows headroom at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They sell 100.0% traded goods — zero manufacturing — so their price includes a reseller margin. Market research shows PP caps asking ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with ₹0.65–0.80 possible at higher volume. Push them to pass through the maker's price or introduce us to their upstream source.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Ask to stretch from 30 days to 45 days
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 45 days frees up about ₹5.36 L of cash for us (plus another ₹2.68 L for the extra 15 days)

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.8% as profit (similar firms keep 3.1%), so there's little room to squeeze on price without hurting supply. But they take 105 days to pay their own suppliers — way longer than the 57 days similar firms take — so asking them to give us more time is only fair. We're 1.19% of their ₹54.69 Cr revenue, a real chunk, so they'll want to keep us. Their money-health score is weak (2/10) and they're in the grey distress zone (Altman Z 1.58), so don't push so hard you tip them over — focus on terms and lining up a second source.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Top second-source candidate and a direct manufacturer, so no reseller margin.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging. Strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: Their weak money-health (2/10) and grey-zone distress signal mean supply could wobble — don't put all your eggs in this basket; qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek now.
They have pending legal case(s) flagged — ask what those are and whether they affect operations or cashflow.
Pushing too hard on price (given the thin 2.8% profit) could break them and leave you scrambling for supply mid-year.
They're a trader, not a maker — if their upstream source hikes price or cuts them off, your price and supply are at risk. Ask who manufactures for them and consider going direct.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about stretching payment to 45 days — you already give your own suppliers 105 days, so that's fair — and getting closer to a manufacturer's price, since we know you're reselling these caps.
